gen-gf-gabarito-gf-ruluko: Expressive from the first glance, Gabarito cuts its terminals open so counters flow outward, while Ruluko keeps broad open bowls. Big, short headings are where Gabarito earns its place.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tasa-orbiter: A line you can trace: Gabarito keeps its outline constant. TASA Orbiter keeps every small counter unclogged, so text set in it stays crisp from the first paragraph to the last.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tirra: Gabarito stitches its strokes like thread along a path, with open-cut terminals that let the counters flow outward. But Tirra, with round forms like open parentheses, supplies the modern counterweight that lets the heading's personality stand out.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-titillium-web: Titillium Web keeps its stroke ends set far apart, giving a contemporary, approachable text face under Gabarito's heading. And over many lines the open stroke ends keep the text moving smoothly, never tiring against Gabarito's uniform strokes.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tomorrow: A single-nib drawn look defines Gabarito, with terminals cut open so counters flow outward. Tomorrow shapes its bowls like a cupped palm of clay, a clean foil for that display voice.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Drawn as if with one nib, Gabarito opens its terminals so counters flow outward. Tsukimi Rounded brings round forms like open parentheses and parallel stroke edges, so the two meet smoothly on a page.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-tuffy: Loose, sketched, unmistakable: Tuffy draws letters with a pencil that never presses harder, and its s opens wide. But Gabarito earns its keep when big and short, where its open-cut terminals can flow.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-urbanist: Expressive down to its open-cut terminals, Gabarito does its best work as display type. Urbanist does the quieter job, its broad-nibbed stroke never curling shut across contemporary, steady text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-varta: Gabarito draws vertical and horizontal strokes at identical weight, with terminals cut open. Varta does the opposite job, handing every e and a a big open eye so running text stays friendly and legible.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-ysabeau-office: Ysabeau Office reads open-ended, with every curved letter left unclosed. Gabarito's ruler-and-compass line gives the heading its crisp snap, and the two sit together on the page without friction.
